title: Frontend: copy idempotency on the plant records port — Idempotency-Key in real + stub, records-port contract tests, rendering contract for the Copy button (R4)
recipe: No recipe covers a records adapter (SIBLING-SET-PLAN §8 G-D). The script is a TRANSPOSITION of the live-animals implementation named file-by-file in notes, per Sam's ruling R4. NOTE THE TRANSPOSITION: live-animals implements idempotency on the FULFILMENT resource (POST /fulfilments/{id}/copy); plant-products puts /copies on the NOTIFICATION resource (POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies). Transpose the pattern, not the code.

filesToTouch.what: Change the copy op from `copy(journeyId)` to `copy(journeyId, idempotencyKey)` and send the header. Exemplar to mirror: services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js:15-20, where copy issues the POST with `'Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey` merged into the request headers alongside the existing content-type and tracing headers. Plant form: POST `${notificationsUrl}/${journeyId}/copies` with headers { 'content-type': 'application/json', [tracingHeader]: …, 'Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey }, expect 201, return marshal(body). ADD A LOCAL GUARD BEFORE THE FETCH: if idempotencyKey is nullish or, after String(...).trim(), empty, throw new Error('records.copy requires an idempotencyKey') — do NOT let a keyless copy reach the network. That guard is load-bearing beyond hygiene: it is what makes it impossible for pp-045 to ship a Copy button that mints no key (the backend would 400, but a local throw fails in unit tests rather than only in an integration run). This edit CLOSES pp-008's recorded open question 'POST …/copies has no Idempotency-Key support' — pp-054 adds it to the backend, so the frontend now sends it.

Change the stub's copy op to `copy(journeyId, idempotencyKey)` with a dedupe map, mirroring services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/create.js:22-27 exactly. Add a module-level `copiesBySourceAndKey = new Map()` beside the existing journeys store (and clear it in clear(), which the stub already exposes as a test hook). Behaviour: build `const dedupeKey = `${journeyId}\u0000${idempotencyKey}`` — the NUL separator is deliberate and is the live-animals form; it makes the composite key unambiguous for any journeyId/key pair. If copiesBySourceAndKey has that dedupeKey, return a structuredClone of the ALREADY-MADE copy and make no new record. Otherwise run the existing copy path (source lookup, copyable-status guard, mint a fresh GBN-PP reference, fresh DRAFT, cloned content, no submittedAt/submittedSnapshot — documentless per D-19), then copiesBySourceAndKey.set(dedupeKey, newRecord.journeyId) before returning. Apply the SAME blank-key guard as real.js (throw before any store read) so the two impls fail identically — that identity is what the port contract suite asserts.

Add the two R4 contract cases to the dual-implementation suite pp-008 created (the suite already runs one shared spec against BOTH the stub and the network-mocked real impl — add these inside it so both impls are held to them):
(1) 'one new draft per idempotency key' — create a source, transition it to a copyable status, call copy(sourceRef, key) TWICE with the same key, assert both calls return the SAME journeyId and that a subsequent list() shows exactly ONE draft copy of that source. Not 'copy was called once' — assert the observable record count, because that is the behaviour the backend index enforces.
(2) 'copy idempotency scoped to the source reference' — with the same key value, copy(sourceA, key) and copy(sourceB, key) must yield DISTINCT journeyIds, each derived from its own source. READ THE OPEN QUESTION BEFORE WRITING THIS ONE: the plant BACKEND (pp-054) dedupes on the key ALONE, matching live-animals, while the stub's `${journeyId}\u0000${key}` composite is source-scoped. The two agree in production only because a key is minted fresh per rendered action per source, so the same key never reaches two sources. Resolution for this suite: assert source scoping against the STUB, and for the real impl assert the weaker, true statement — that the request carries the key and the path carries the source reference, so the server can scope however it chooses. Mark the divergence with a comment naming pp-054's openQuestion so the next person does not 'fix' the stub to match a backend that may itself change.
Also add: copy() with a missing/blank key rejects in BOTH impls before any request or store write.

Add to the network-boundary op→HTTP suite: the copy request carries an `Idempotency-Key` header whose value is exactly the argument passed (assert on the captured fetch init, not on a spy call count); the header is present alongside the existing content-type and tracing headers; and copy() with a nullish or whitespace-only key throws WITHOUT issuing a fetch (assert the fetch mock recorded zero calls — 'did not go to the network' is the behaviour under test).

Add to the stub-only suite: repeating copy(sourceRef, key) with the same key returns the same journeyId and leaves the store size unchanged; two different keys against one source yield two distinct drafts; clear() empties the dedupe map as well as the journeys store (otherwise a later test inherits a stale copy and fails mysteriously); a blank key throws before any store mutation.

Add a short '## Copy idempotency' section to the set charter recording the RENDERING CONTRACT that the Copy button must follow when pp-045 ships it, so the requirement survives outside this increment's diff. State it as four rules, each naming its live-animals exemplar: (1) a `randomUUID()` from node:crypto is minted PER RENDERED COPY ACTION — per row on the dashboard, per render of the review page — never once per module load and never once per process (exemplars: features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:1,22 mints inside the per-row action builder; features/check-answers/controller.js:1,73 takes `copyIdempotencyKey = randomUUID()` as a defaulted option so a re-render can pass the SAME key back in); (2) the key rides the form as a hidden input named exactly `idempotencyKey` (exemplars: the dashboard and check-answers template.njk files); (3) the copy POST controller reads `request.payload?.idempotencyKey?.trim()` and passes it as the fourth argument of `copyJourney(request, h, journeyId, idempotencyKey)` — the L2 engine seam already carries it (engine/journey.js:125, verified; NO L2 change is needed for plant-products); (4) the recoverable-error path re-renders with the SAME key, not a new one, so a user retrying after a 500 gets the copy that may already have been made (exemplar: features/notification-actions/controller.js:12-24, recoverCopy). Add a FIFTH rule (R7 — symmetric mounts): the Copy button's form ACTION and its post-copy REDIRECT are prefix-BEARING LINKS, built with pagePath()/hubPath()/dashboardPath(), never route-shape builders and never a hand-written path. The live-animals exemplar being transposed (features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js) emits paths for a set that is ITSELF prefixed now, so a bare `/notifications/…` or a bare `'/'` copied across would be wrong for BOTH sets — under FD-18 a bare '/' would even 302 the user into live-animals after copying a plant draft. Say this in the charter so pp-045's planner meets it before writing the action. Also record that sets/plant-products/services/records/{real,stub}.js THROW on a missing key, so a Copy button that forgets rule 1 fails in unit tests rather than silently double-creating.

schemaFields: Idempotency-Key (request header on POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies — minted client-side, never persisted in the answers tree, never part of any PUT body)
specs: NONE new — service-layer increment with no UI surface. Coverage is unit-level: records-port.test.js (the two R4 contract cases, run against both impls), real.test.js (header on the wire, no-fetch on a blank key), stub.test.js (dedupe, distinct keys, clear resets).
acceptanceCriteria: sets/plant-products/services/records/real.js copy(journeyId, idempotencyKey) sends an Idempotency-Key request header carrying exactly the supplied value, alongside the existing content-type and tracing headers, against POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies.

Both real.js and stub.js reject a nullish, empty or whitespace-only idempotencyKey by throwing BEFORE any network call or store mutation — proven by asserting zero fetch calls / unchanged store size, not by a spy on the guard.

stub.js dedupes on `${journeyId}\u0000${idempotencyKey}`: a repeated (source, key) pair returns the already-made copy and creates no second record; clear() resets the dedupe map as well as the journeys store.

records-port.test.js pins 'one new draft per idempotency key' against BOTH impls by asserting the observable record count after two identical copy calls, and pins 'copy idempotency scoped to the source reference' with the stub/real divergence explicitly documented in the test rather than papered over.

The plant records port's copy op is signature-compatible with the L2 engine seam copyJourney(request, h, journeyId, idempotencyKey) → records.copy(journeyId, idempotencyKey) (engine/journey.js:125) — no L2 file is edited by this increment.

sets/plant-products/docs/README.md records the FIVE-rule rendering contract (per-rendered-action randomUUID; hidden input named idempotencyKey; controller passes it as the fourth copyJourney argument; recovery re-renders with the SAME key; and — R7 — the form action and post-copy redirect are prefix-BEARING links built with pagePath()/hubPath()/dashboardPath(), never route-shape builders and never a hand-written '/notifications/…' or bare '/') with its live-animals exemplar for each rule.

pp-008's recorded open question — 'POST …/copies has no Idempotency-Key support … a double-submitted copy action can mint two drafts' — is closed, and the closure is noted where that question was raised.

P-2 containment holds: no file under sets/plant-products/ imports anything from services/persistence/records/; npm run lint (which runs lint:arch) is green with no dependency-cruiser baseline regeneration.

Sibling safety in its co-residency form (R7): npm test, npm run test:live-animals, npm run test:plant-products and the Playwright suites are green with no test-count drop, and BOTH sets still serve correctly from ONE process under their OWN prefixes — live-animals at /live-animals, plant-products at /plant-products. 'live-animals is unchanged' is not the bar and no longer means anything.
No Copy button, form or route is added by this increment — the rendered action is pp-045's, and it is now impossible for pp-045 to ship one without a key because the port throws.
verification: npm --prefix ~/git/defra/trade-imports-animals/repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend run test:plant-products  # baseline BEFORE editing — red baseline = stop and report
notes:
AMENDED FOR RULING R7 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session) — SYMMETRIC MOUNTS. One small but real consequence for this increment, and it is entirely in the charter contract rather than in the adapter code: the Copy button's form ACTION and its post-copy REDIRECT are prefix-BEARING LINKS (pagePath/hubPath/dashboardPath), not route shapes. The live-animals file being transposed (features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js) now emits `/live-animals/…` rather than the bare `/notifications/…` it emitted when live-animals sat at the root, so a literal copy-across would be wrong for both sets — and a bare '/' redirect would 302 a user who just copied a PLANT draft into live-animals (FD-18). The charter gains that as rule 5 so pp-045's planner meets it. Nothing about the Idempotency-Key work itself changes: headers, dedupe keys and the port contract are URL-agnostic.

RULING R4 (Sam, 2026-08-01): copy idempotency matches what live-animals already does, exactly, on both sides, and is sequenced BEFORE the Copy button ships. pp-054 is the backend half; this is the frontend half. BOTH must land before pp-045 (draft lifecycle), which is the increment that renders the Copy button — say this in pp-045's body when it is planned, and treat a Copy action arriving without both as a build-loop halt.

SCOPE SPLIT AND WHY (headless decision, recorded not asked). The orchestrator's brief for this increment names four things: randomUUID per rendered copy action, the hidden idempotencyKey input, the Idempotency-Key header in the adapter, and the records-port contract tests. Only the last two can be BUILT here, because there is no rendered copy action in the plant set yet: pp-037 (dashboard, full build) explicitly limits pass-1 row actions to Continue-into-hub and defers delete/amend/copy-as-new to pp-045, and pp-045 is one of the m5 increments that ruling R5 says stay unplanned stubs — so this increment must not plan it. The resolution is not to drop the rendering half but to make it UNSKIPPABLE: real.js and stub.js both throw on a missing key, so any future Copy button that forgets to mint one fails in unit tests, and the four-rule rendering contract is written into the set charter (sets/plant-products/docs/README.md) where pp-045's planner will read it. If Sam would rather see the rendered action built now, the change is to pull the dashboard copy row action forward out of pp-045 into this increment — flagged, not assumed.

READ THESE LIVE-ANIMALS FILES FIRST — the reference implementation, all verified live this session:
- services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js:15-20 — copy(journeyId, idempotencyKey) and the 'Idempotency-Key' header
- services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/create.js:22-49 — the `${journeyId}\u0000${idempotencyKey}` dedupe key, the copiesBySourceAndKey map, return-the-existing-clone on a repeat
- engine/journey.js:125-127 — copyJourney(request, h, journeyId, idempotencyKey) → records.copy(journeyId, idempotencyKey) (the L2 seam ALREADY carries the key; nothing in L2 changes)
- sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:1,22 — randomUUID() minted inside the per-row action builder
- sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/controller.js:1,55,73 — `copyIdempotencyKey = randomUUID()` as a defaulted render option, surfaced to the view as idempotencyKey
- sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/notification-actions/controller.js:12-39 — request.payload?.idempotencyKey?.trim(), the recoverCopy path that re-renders with the SAME key, and the redirect-to-hub-or-dashboard outcome
- services/persistence/records/records-port.test.js — the dual-impl contract-suite pattern the plant suite copies

TESTING RULES THAT APPLY HERE: test behaviour, not implementation — assert record counts and captured request init, never toHaveBeenCalled on internal helpers; mock at the NETWORK boundary (global fetch) and never module-mock; do not add a test per status enum value. The one sanctioned call-assertion is 'zero fetch calls' / 'store size unchanged' on the blank-key path, because 'did not write' IS the behaviour.

DEPENDENCY NOTE: dependsOn pp-008 (which creates real.js, stub.js, records-port.test.js, real.test.js and stub.test.js — this increment only edits them) and pp-054 (which adds the backend header; without it the real adapter would send a header the server ignores and the contract would be untested end to end).
openQuestions: Scoping divergence to keep visible: the backend (pp-054, live-animals parity) dedupes on the KEY ALONE, while the stub dedupes on (source, key). They are indistinguishable in production only because a key is minted per rendered action per source. The port contract test documents the divergence rather than hiding it. If pp-054's own open question resolves toward a server-side compound (referenceNumber, copyIdempotencyKey) index, the stub is already right and only the real-impl assertion tightens.

Whether the rendered copy action should be pulled forward out of pp-045 into this increment so R4's 'both sides' is literally complete in one commit. Planned as NO (pp-037 defers copy actions; R5 forbids planning the m5 stubs), with the port throw plus the charter contract as the enforcement. Reversible with one decision from Sam.
